_comment: Which schema paths this cross-reader check can and cannot reach, and why.
Derived by walking IHP-GmbH/chiplet-spec schemas/chiplet.schema.json and
resolving every $ref, so the corpus is bounded by the schema rather than by
what somebody remembered to list. 89 addressable paths: 88 leaves plus the
second form of the components[].cells oneOf, which is addressable as a scalar
and as a sequence and is therefore two paths, not one.
The first version of this file listed 53 paths and claimed 42 of 42 reachable.
That was wrong in both directions. It was assembled by hand and it silently
dropped six string paths the writer really does emit (the three under
technologies.<id> and the three under connection_stacks.<id>), because both
reach the same $ref the interconnect block reaches and a hand walk counted the
definition once instead of counting each route. It also never said what the
other 35 paths were, so a reader could not tell an out-of-scope path from a
forgotten one. Every path is now in exactly one bucket and the buckets sum to
the whole schema. cross_reader_check.py asserts both of those rather than
taking this file's word for them.
emitted            this host's writer can produce it, and it is string-typed,
so YAML 1.1 vs 1.2 scalar resolution decides whether the
other reader gets a string back. This is what the check is
for. Every one of these must have an expectation.
canonicalized      the writer chooses the form: one cell is written as
top_cell, several as cells. Both forms are covered.
unsupported        the model has nowhere to put it, so the writer cannot emit
it and no fixture can make it appear. Adding a fixture
value here would force adding model support to satisfy a
test, which is the test driving the product. An expectation
naming one of these is a failure, on purpose.
non_string         numbers and booleans. Quoting is not the question for these
and quoting them would be wrong. What IS a question for the
numeric ones is integer-vs-float: yaml-cpp writes 2000.0 as
2000, and PyYAML then hands its caller an int where the
other reader had a double. The four paths an import
actually emits moved to numeric below; the 24 that
remain here are NOT covered by this check.
numeric            the four non-string paths writeSingleGdsImport really
emits. Pinned by declared Python type and by value, so a
change in how the writer formats a number reddens a test
instead of drifting silently. Pinning is not endorsing:
the schema declares number for all four and PyYAML gets an
int for three of them. Recording that is this bucket's job;
see tests/CROSS_READER_CHECK.md.
undeclared_value_type  components[].metadata is additionalProperties: true
with no declared value type, so it has no schema path to
address. The writer does emit its values as quoted strings.
Not covered, and not coverable this way.
opaque             flow is bytes the format tells hosts not to interpret. The
studio re-emits the source slice verbatim, so there is no
re-serialisation for a reader to disagree about.
Two coverage claims, and they stay two. 48 of 48 reachable string paths
(46 emitted + 2 canonicalized), and 4 of 28 numeric paths. Adding them is
the error to avoid: the numeric four were chosen because an import emits
them, not as a sample of the 28, so a combined figure would read as progress
across a corpus nobody is working through. Out of 89 addressable either way.
NOT 52 of 89, and not 42 of 42.
schema_sha256_note: sha256 of schemas/chiplet.schema.json as this classification was derived. Recorded because the derivation ran against a local chiplet-spec WORKING TREE, and a working tree is not the sha it sits on. Verified equal to `git show 3340e113ceae102cae2c0ace747f4ecb408da0bf:schemas/chiplet.schema.json` at the time of writing. Re-derive against a moved checkout and this hash is how you find out.
addressable_total_note: Number of addressable paths in the schema named above. The buckets must sum to exactly this; cross_reader_check.py asserts it. Moving a path between buckets leaves it alone, which is right, because that is a reclassification and not a change in what the schema contains. Losing a path lowers it and reddens the check.
